questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’**.

Sele, is a near extinct language, __spoken for __just five villages in Nepal, which lie close to Tibet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Spoken in'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **In the underlined part,** **'For' preposition** is incorrect because it is used for the following things:-

 
 
• To show reason or cause 
 
• having as a destination
 
• representing something.
 
• Affecting or with regard to.
 
 
 
• *Hence, **none of the usages of 'for'** connect with the other statement which is written after the preposition hence this needs to be improved.*
 
• **'In'** preposition is correct because it is used to **show an enclosed space or a place that is surrounded by boundaries.**
 
• **In the given sentence, 'Villages' **are the enclosed spaces 2-dimensional spaces hence with 2-D objects always use the preposition 'in'
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• The dog is in the garden. (Garden is the 2-D space.)
 
 

**So the correct sentence is**→ *Sele, is a near-extinct language, **spoken in** just five villages in Nepal, which lie close to Tibet. *

Ravi asked, “Ritu, how many sets of class 12 practice papers have you finished?”

options.text: Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers had she been finishing.
Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers she had finished.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '2' i.e. 'Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers she had finished.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the rule of Direct-Indirect speech,** Whenever the tense in the reported speech is the present perfect tense convert this tense into the past perfect tense.
 
• In the given Options there is only one option which is given in the past perfect tense which is option 2.
 
• Option 1→ is incorrect because it is written in the past perfect continuous tense which is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Reporting Verb** →The first verb part of the sentence that comes before the quotation marks are called the Reporting verb. 

**Reported Speech**→ The statement (words) spoken by the speaker and which is written in quotation marks (“ ”) is called the Reported speech.

 
• *Present tense changed into→ a Past tense*
 
• *If the Reported speech is a universal truth or a general fact, then its ‘tense’ does not change irrespective of the Reporting verb.*
 
• *Present continuous tense changed into→past continuous tense.*
 
• *Present Perfect Changes into→ Past Perfect*
 
• *Present Perfect Continuous Changes into→ Past Perfect Continuous*

• **Sentence D-** will be the second sentence because '**but' conjunction** is used **to show the contrast **or this sentence is opposing sentence C also, it tells what happens after constructing the clinics.
